examples.solution_text:
For $\theta$, the opposite side is $p$, the adjacent side is $q$ and the hypotenuse is $r$.

$\sin\theta=\dfrac{p}{r},\qquad\cos\theta=\dfrac{q}{r}$

For $90^{\circ}-\theta$, the opposite side is $q$ and the hypotenuse is $r$.

$\begin{aligned}\sin(90^{\circ}-\theta)&=\dfrac{q}{r}\\&=\cos\theta\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Rewrite (a) $\sin34^{\circ}$ as a cosine and (b) $\cos65^{\circ}$ as a sine.

examples.solution_text:
$\cos47^{\circ}=\sin43^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{-\sin43^{\circ}}{\cos47^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{-\sin43^{\circ}}{\sin43^{\circ}}\\&=-1\end{aligned}$

The denominator is nonzero because $43^{\circ}$ is acute.

$\cos27^{\circ}=\sin63^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{2\cos27^{\circ}+3\sin63^{\circ}}{4\sin63^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{2\sin63^{\circ}+3\sin63^{\circ}}{4\sin63^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{5\sin63^{\circ}}{4\sin63^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{5}{4}\end{aligned}$

The denominator is nonzero because $63^{\circ}$ is acute.

$\cos66^{\circ}=\sin24^{\circ}$ and $\sin66^{\circ}=\cos24^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{\sin24^{\circ}}{\cos66^{\circ}}+\dfrac{\cos24^{\circ}}{\sin66^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{\sin24^{\circ}}{\sin24^{\circ}}+\dfrac{\cos24^{\circ}}{\cos24^{\circ}}\\&=1+1\\&=2\end{aligned}$

Both denominators are nonzero because $24^{\circ}$ is acute.

examples.derivation: Relative to theta, opposite=p, adjacent=q and hypotenuse=r. Thus sin(theta)=p/r and cos(theta)=q/r. The complementary angle has opposite=q, so sin(90°−theta)=q/r=cos(theta). AC has direction atan2(−3,4)=323.13° from A, matching the corrected arc endpoint; the two acute angles are 53.13° and 36.87°.
sin37°=cos53°. Cosine is one-to-one on acute angles, so cos(theta)=cos53° gives theta=53°.
29°+61°=90°, so cos29°=sin61°. Subtracting the equal ratios gives 0.
47°+43°=90°, so cos47°=sin43°>0. Hence −sin43°/cos47°=−1. The adaptation correctly uses complementary angles rather than the source's mismatched pair.
cos27°=sin63°. Writing s=sin63°>0, the expression becomes (2s+3s)/(4s)=5/4.
36°+54°=90°, so cos54°=sin36°. The product is sin36°×sin36°=sin²36°.
cos66°=sin24° and sin66°=cos24°. Both are positive, so the two quotients each equal 1 and their sum equals 2.
